title: Domain-driven design offers a practical map for coding agents in legacy systems
friendlyTitle: Clear project maps can help coding agents work in old codebases
summary: A practitioner argues that coding agents struggle in mature systems when business language, ownership and boundaries are unclear. The proposed workflow records bounded contexts, glossaries, dependencies and required checks, leaving humans to make strategic design decisions while agents execute reviewed tactical work.
friendlySummary: Coding agents often guess badly when a large project uses unclear names and boundaries. This guide shows how to document the business language, ownership and checks an agent needs.
whyItMatters: Better models do not automatically fix ambiguous codebases. Teams can improve agent output by documenting the concepts and boundaries that experienced engineers normally carry in their heads, then using tests and reviews to constrain implementation.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Clearer project knowledge can reduce wrong changes while keeping important design decisions with people.
